name: SwipeBy
description: Independent restaurants get a website, online ordering and loyalty program for free. Revenue comes from the marketing layer on top: social media management, reputation management, phone answering, remarketing and AI-generated print campaigns (company-stated).

mentions.evidence: ARR $3.5M, +400% YoY ACV ~$6K, mostly prepaid annually · $0 ad spend · 300–400 demos/month 25 staff (3 engineers) · reps have a quota of 6 locations/month on 30–40% commission $450K revenue-based financing from Founderpath (~$35K/mo repayments, 16-month payback) · EBITDA ~0% · says he turned down a $15M all-cash offer
mentions.indieAngle: "Free site, paid marketing retainer, sold in person" works in any Polish city. Pick one vertical (kebab/pizzerie, barbers, warsztaty), give away the Pyszne-alternative ordering page, and charge 300–600 zł/mo for Google reviews + GBP posts + SMS remarketing. One salesperson can cover a city.

whyItPrints: It's old-school local-SMB selling. Every customer comes from field reps physically walking into restaurants, there are no free trials, and customers mostly prepay annually. The founder argues the in-person relationship is the moat AI cold-callers can't copy.
whyThisMatters:
An independent restaurant gets a website, online ordering, and a loyalty program without paying for them. The bill is the marketing on top: social posts, reviews, a phone answering service, remarketing, and printed campaigns. Every customer, the founder says, comes from a person walking into the restaurant. There is no free trial. Most of them pay for the year up front.

He says the yearly number is a few million, with no ad spend, and a few hundred demos a month. Twenty-five people, three of them engineers. Reps have a quota of a handful of locations a month. There is revenue-based financing to repay. He says he turned down an all-cash offer. That is his interview, recorded in September 2026. It is not a Stripe connection. The real site is swipe.by. A similar domain is parked and is not this company.

You pay a local shop so the Google listing and the reviews are someone else's Tuesday.
